full_text_en:
Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd. v. Sino-Environment Technology Group Limited — dispute over shareholders' capital contribution

[Ruling Summary]

In accordance with Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, matters such as the obligation to make capital contributions between a foreign-invested enterprise in China and its foreign investor shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China; matters such as the civil capacity for rights and the civil capacity for conduct of the judicial administrator and liquidator of the foreign investor shall be governed by the laws of the place where the foreign investor is registered.

Article 13 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides that changes to the legal representative of a company shall be registered with the relevant authorities. The registration of a change of legal representative serves to publicly disclose the basic status of the company's authority to represent its will. The legally registered legal representative with the administrative authorities for industry and commerce has external effect; if an external dispute involving a third party outside the company arises due to the company's representation authority, the registration with the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall prevail. However, for internal disputes between the company and its shareholders arising from the appointment or removal of the legal representative, the valid resolution of the shareholders' meeting for appointment or removal shall prevail, and the legal effect of the change of legal representative shall take effect within the company.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling

(2014) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 20

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sino-Environment Technology Group Limited (SINO-ENVIRONMENT TECHNOLOGY GROUP LIMITED). Domicile: One Raffles Palace #10-62, Singapore 048616, Republic of Singapore.

Representative: Hamish Alexander Christie, Liquidator of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Dan Pingyuan, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhengjian Yongshen Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Deng Huiqiong, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhengjian Yongshen Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd. Domicile: Main Building, Fujian Torch High-Tech Innovation Park, No. 611 Gongye Road, Gulou District, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Hong Zhen, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Deng Zhihuang, Attorney at Law, Fujian Zhixinheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xia Xiaoli, Attorney at Law, Fujian Zhixinheng Law Firm.

The appellant, Sino-Environment Technology Group Limited (hereinafter referred to as Environmental Technology Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2013) Min Min Chu Zi No. 43 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Fujian High Court) on December 18, 2013, in the case of a dispute over shareholders' capital contribution between the appellant and the appellee, Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Thumb Company). After accepting the case, this court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on June 11, 2014. The agents ad litem of Environmental Technology Company, Dan Pingyuan and Deng Huiqiong, and the agents ad litem of Thumb Company, Deng Zhihuang and Xia Xiaoli, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Thumb Company filed a lawsuit with the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Fuzhou Intermediate Court) on April 27, 2012, alleging: Thumb Company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established in China by Environmental Technology Company, which is registered in Singapore. It obtained its business license on June 30, 2000, with a registered capital of RMB 130 million (the same currency applies below). On June 30, 2008, Thumb Company's registered capital was approved to increase to RMB 380 million, with the increased portion to be fully paid in installments by August 3, 2010. As of May 19, 2009, the paid-in registered capital was RMB 185,221,300, and Environmental Technology Company had not made further payments thereafter. On August 18, 2010, Thumb Company filed a separate lawsuit with Fuzhou Intermediate Court, requesting Environmental Technology Company to pay an interim capital increase of RMB 49 million. After the judgment in that case became effective, Environmental Technology Company paid RMB 49,395,110.4 on October 31, 2011. As of that date, the actual capital contribution paid by Environmental Technology Company was RMB 234,616,431.4, with an outstanding capital increase payment of RMB 45,383,568.6. Accordingly, Thumb Company requested the court to order Environmental Technology Company to fulfill its shareholder capital contribution obligation and pay the capital increase of RMB 45 million. After Fuzhou Intermediate Court accepted the case, Environmental Technology Company raised a jurisdictional objection. Fuzhou Intermediate Court ruled to dismiss the objection. Environmental Technology Company appealed against that ruling, and Fujian High Court issued a civil ruling (2013) Min Min Zhong Zi No. 357, assigning the case to its own jurisdiction.

The Fujian High Court found the following facts upon trial:

Thumb Company was approved by the Fujian Provincial People's Government through the document Shang Wai Zi [2004] No. 0009 in 2004 and obtained the Certificate of Approval for Enterprises with Foreign Investment of the People's Republic of China. Its enterprise type was a limited liability company wholly owned by a foreign legal person. Since its establishment, the company's name, domicile, legal representative, shareholder name, total investment, and registered capital had undergone several changes. Since September 2005, the sole shareholder of the company has been Environmental Technology Company. On December 18, 2012, the registered legal representative of Thumb Company was changed to Hong Zhen.

On June 30, 2008, the Fujian Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation issued the document Min Wai Jing Mao Zi [2008] No. 251, "Reply on Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd.'s Increase of Investment," approving Thumb Company's total investment to increase from RMB 230 million to RMB 500 million, and its registered capital from RMB 130 million to RMB 380 million. The increased portion was to be contributed within the time limit specified in the company's revised articles of association. The reply also approved the "Supplemental Articles of Association" executed by Thumb Company for the above changes. The "Supplemental Articles of Association" stated the following regarding the capital increase amount and payment time: the entire capital increase was to be made by Environmental Technology Company in the form of foreign exchange cash, with an initial payment of no less than 20% of the new registered capital, and the balance to be paid in full within two years from the date of issuance of the revised business license.

On July 16, 2008, Environmental Technology Company paid the first installment of the capital increase of RMB 50,560,381 to Thumb Company; on May 19, 2009, Environmental Technology Company paid the second installment of the capital increase of RMB 4,660,940 to Thumb Company. As of that date, Thumb Company's paid-in registered capital was RMB 185,221,300. On August 18, 2010, Thumb Company filed a separate lawsuit with Fuzhou Intermediate Court, requesting an order for Environmental Technology Company to make an interim payment of the capital increase of RMB 49 million. Fuzhou Intermediate Court ruled in favor of Thumb Company's claim. Environmental Technology Company appealed, and Fujian High Court, on August 31, 2011, issued a civil judgment (2011) Min Min Zhong Zi No. 446 (hereinafter referred to as case No. 446), dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Environmental Technology Company paid the capital increase of RMB 49,395,110.4 on October 31, 2011, in accordance with the effective judgment. On March 12, 2012, Thumb Company completed the registration of the change of its business license. After the change, Thumb Company's registered capital was RMB 380 million, and its paid-in capital was RMB 234,616,431.4. As of July 25, 2013, Environmental Technology Company still had an outstanding capital contribution of RMB 145,383,568.6 to Thumb Company.

On May 31, 2012, Fuzhou Intermediate Court, upon Thumb Company's application, issued a civil ruling (2012) Rong Min Chu Zi No. 252-1, preserving RMB 45 million of Environmental Technology Company's bank deposits. On November 22, 2013, Fujian High Court, at Thumb Company's request, issued a civil ruling (2013) Min Min Chu Zi No. 43-1, continuing the preservation of Environmental Technology Company's property with a total value not exceeding RMB 45 million.

The court further found:

Environmental Technology Company was registered in Singapore in 2001 as a public company limited by shares. On June 4, 2010, the High Court of Singapore issued a court order, upon the application of Environmental Technology Company, placing the company under judicial management, appointing Mr. Seshadri Rajogpalan and Ms. Ee Meng Yen Angela as joint and several judicial managers of Environmental Technology Company to manage the company's daily affairs, business, and property, for the purpose of reorganizing the company or retaining its business in whole or in part for sustainable operation, and/or achieving a more advantageous realization of the company's assets than would be achieved through liquidation.

On March 1, 2012, the High Court of Singapore issued a court order, upon the application of the judicial managers of Environmental Technology Company, Seshadri Rajogpalan and Ee Meng Yen Angela, extending the judicial management order made on June 4, 2010, to May 2, 2012, approving the resignation of Seshadri Rajogpalan and Ee Meng Yen Angela as judicial managers of Environmental Technology Company, and appointing Hamish Alexander Christie as judicial manager of Environmental Technology Company effective from the date of the order, including the power to continue any litigation or legal proceedings initiated by the former judicial managers in the original summons.

The "Legal Opinion" on the judicial management system under the Singapore Companies Act provided by Tanglin Law Corporation of Singapore in case No. 446 stated: 1. The judicial management procedure under the Singapore Companies Act involves a person applying to the High Court of Singapore to place a company under judicial management. The purpose of the judicial management system is to provide companies that are unable to pay their debts as they fall due with a breathing space, allowing them an opportunity under supervision to restore their financial health or better realize the value of their assets, rather than being placed directly into liquidation. 2. If the High Court of Singapore considers that a company is or will be unable to pay its debts as they fall due, and that making a court order would have a reasonable prospect of achieving one or more of the following purposes: the survival of the company, or the whole or any part of its undertaking as a going concern; the approval of a compromise or arrangement under the Singapore Companies Act between the company and its creditors; or a more advantageous realization of the company's assets than would be effected through liquidation, the High Court may make a judicial management order in respect of the company. 3. During the period when a judicial management order is in force, no resolution may be passed or order made for the winding up of the company.

On May 16, 2012, Environmental Technology Company filed a lawsuit with Fuzhou Intermediate Court against Thumb Company, Tian Yuan, Chen Bin, and Pan Cheng Tu in a dispute concerning the company, requesting confirmation that the resolutions of Environmental Technology Company appointing and removing the directors, supervisors, and legal representative of Thumb Company were lawful and valid. Fuzhou Intermediate Court rendered a first-instance judgment (2012) Rong Min Chu Zi No. 268 (hereinafter referred to as case No. 268) on September 17, 2013, holding: 1. The "Written Resolution" and "Appointment and Removal Letter" made by Environmental Technology Company on March 30, 2012, are valid; 2. Thumb Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, complete the registration and filing procedures for the change of legal representative, chairman, and directors, and change Thumb Company's legal representative and chairman to Cosimo Borrelli, and directors to Cosimo Borrelli, Xu Liwen, and Song Kuan; 3. Dismiss the other claims of Environmental Technology Company.

On May 7, 2013, Environmental Technology Company filed a lawsuit with the Gulou District People's Court of Fuzhou City (hereinafter referred to as Gulou District Court) against the Fujian Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce and Thumb Company, seeking to set aside the change of Thumb Company's legal representative from Tian Yuan to Hong Zhen and the relevant administrative registration. The case number was (2013) Gu Xing Chu Zi No. 167 (hereinafter referred to as case No. 167). Gulou District Court ruled on March 20, 2014, to suspend the proceedings, reasoning that the case required the outcome of case No. 268 (2012) Rong Min Chu Zi No. 268.

On June 26, 2013, Environmental Technology Company filed a lawsuit with Fuzhou Intermediate Court against Sun Jiangrong and Hong Zhen, seeking an order for them to cease infringement, apologize, eliminate adverse effects, and compensate for losses arising from their unauthorized change of Thumb Company's legal representative from Tian Yuan to Hong Zhen. The case number was (2013) Rong Min Chu Zi No. 753 (hereinafter referred to as case No. 753).

On November 28, 2012, and July 10, 2013, Cosimo Borrelli, in the capacity of legal representative of Environmental Technology Company, submitted to the Fujian Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce and the Gulou District Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation of Fuzhou City applications concerning the reduction of capital of Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd.

On December 5, 2013, Environmental Technology Company filed a lawsuit with Gulou District Court against the Gulou District Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation of Fuzhou City for failing to perform its statutory duty of administrative approval. The case was accepted by Gulou District Court.

The Fujian High Court held:

This case is a dispute over shareholders' capital contribution. Environmental Technology Company is a foreign legal person registered in Singapore, and therefore this case is a foreign-related civil and commercial case. The place of dispute is Fuzhou City. In accordance with Article 1, paragraph 5, and Article 3, paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on the Centralized Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases, and the Fujian High Court's Provisions on the Centralized Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases in Courts in Fujian Province, this court has jurisdiction over this case. The application of law in this case involves two main aspects: first, matters concerning the civil capacity for rights and civil capacity for conduct of Environmental Technology Company. Since Environmental Technology Company is a legal person registered in Singapore, according to Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, which provides that "matters such as the civil capacity for rights, civil capacity for conduct, organizational structure, and rights and obligations of shareholders of a legal person and its branches shall be governed by the law of the place of registration," the law of Singapore shall apply. Second, Thumb Company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise registered in China and is a Chinese legal person. Environmental Technology Company, as the sole shareholder of Thumb Company, exercises relevant rights and obligations including capital contribution, which shall be governed by Chinese law.

I. Whether Thumb Company's expression of intent in filing this lawsuit is genuine

Thumb Company is a Chinese legal person. Its complaint and the power of attorney authorizing lawyers to participate in the lawsuit are affixed with the company's official seal. Environmental Technology Company does not dispute the authenticity of Thumb Company's official seal. Environmental Technology Company only argues that, as the sole shareholder, it has already replaced the management of Thumb Company, including the legal representative and directors, and that the new "legal representative" of Thumb Company has expressed an intention to withdraw the lawsuit before the court. However, because the actual controller of Thumb Company refuses to hand over the company seal, the new "legal representative" cannot affix the seal to the application for withdrawal, and thus Environmental Technology Company denies that Thumb Company's expression of intent in filing this lawsuit is genuine. This court holds that, under the application of Chinese law, the information registered with the administrative authorities for industry and commerce has the effect of public trust. The determination of Thumb Company's legal representative shall still be based on the registration with the administrative authorities for industry and commerce. In the absence of evidence that Cosimo Borrelli has been registered as the legal representative of Thumb Company, his expression of intent to withdraw the lawsuit on behalf of Thumb Company has no legal effect and therefore is not recognized. The purpose of Thumb Company's lawsuit is to request its sole shareholder to fulfill the capital contribution obligation as determined by the capital increase. Environmental Technology Company, instead of performing the obligation voluntarily, has applied to the relevant authorities for a reduction of capital to offset Thumb Company's claim. There is clearly a conflict of interest between Environmental Technology Company and Thumb Company. Under such circumstances, Thumb Company filed this lawsuit to assert its rights. The complaint and power of attorney are affixed with the company's official seal, which does not violate Chinese law, nor can it be concluded that Thumb Company's filing of this lawsuit is not its genuine expression of intent. Therefore, Environmental Technology Company's defense that Thumb Company's lawsuit has no legal effect is unfounded and is not adopted.

II. Whether this case violates the principle of "res judicata" (no action on the same matter)

After the Fujian Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation approved Thumb Company's application for capital increase through document Min Wai Jing Mao Zi [2008] No. 251 on June 30, 2008, the property rights from the capital increase vested in Thumb Company. In the absence of evidence that Thumb Company's failure to claim the entire capital increase amount in a lump sum would harm the interests of the company or its creditors, Thumb Company, as an independent legal person, has independent civil capacity for rights and has the right to lawfully and in good faith assert its civil rights within the scope of the capital increase and independently determine the amount of the claim. Although Thumb Company filed a lawsuit on August 18, 2010, requesting a capital contribution of RMB 49 million, which was upheld by an effective civil judgment, the factual basis for Thumb Company's current claim for RMB 45 million has changed, as the amount of outstanding capital increase has changed. Moreover, the claim for RMB 49 million and the claim for RMB 45 million in this case are different components of the capital increase under the above-mentioned approval, and the former cannot replace or encompass the latter. Therefore, Thumb Company's lawsuit in this case does not violate the principle of "res judicata."

III. Whether this case should be suspended

Environmental Technology Company argued that this case should be stayed, primarily on the ground that the adjudication of this case needed to be based on the outcomes of the aforementioned Cases No. 268, No. 167, and No. 753. Environmental Technology Company also argued that the adjudication of this case should await the result of its application for capital reduction made in the name of Thumb Company. After the first-instance trial, Environmental Technology Company additionally submitted as evidence litigation materials from its lawsuit against the Gulou District Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau of Fuzhou City for failing to perform its statutory duty of administrative approval, requesting the administrative organ to immediately perform its statutory duty of preliminary examination for the capital reduction of Thumb Company, and persisted in its argument that this case should be stayed. The court held that, with respect to the claims of Environmental Technology Company in the above four cases, the claims in the first three cases were directed to matters such as the appointment, change of registration, and whether there were infringing acts concerning the directors, supervisors, and legal representative of Thumb Company, and had no direct or substantive connection with Environmental Technology Company's capital reduction request. The fourth case was an administrative lawsuit filed by Environmental Technology Company against the capital reduction approval authority for inaction, seeking an order compelling the administrative organ to immediately perform its statutory duty of preliminary examination for capital reduction, not to perform the capital reduction approval procedure. Even if the claim of Environmental Technology Company were upheld, the administrative organ would only perform the statutory duty of preliminary examination, which would not necessarily result in the approval of Thumb Company's capital reduction application. In other words, the capital reduction application of Thumb Company would still require the administrative organ to review and decide whether to approve it in accordance with the law. At present, in the absence of evidence showing that the administrative organ has effectively approved the capital reduction of Thumb Company, the Reply No. Min Wai Jing Mao Zi [2008] 251 issued by the Fujian Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation on June 30, 2008, remains legally effective and should be taken as the basis for deciding the case. Therefore, whatever the outcomes of the four lawsuits filed by Environmental Technology Company, they would not affect Environmental Technology Company's capital contribution obligation in this case, nor would they affect the adjudication of the capital contribution dispute in this case. The adjudication of this case also does not need to await the result of Environmental Technology Company's application for capital reduction made in the name of Thumb Company. This case does not have the circumstances for staying the proceedings as prescribed in Article 150 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Environmental Technology Company's defense argument for staying the proceedings in this case is not supported.

IV. Regarding the issue of capital contribution liability in this case

Environmental Technology Company is a Singapore legal person. It established Thumb Company, a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, within the territory of China. As a shareholder, its capital contribution to Thumb Company shall be governed by Chinese law. Thumb Company's capital increase in 2008 was approved by the foreign investment enterprise approval authority, the Fujian Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation. The capital increase procedure was legal and valid. Environmental Technology Company shall comply with Chinese law and fulfill its capital contribution obligation to Thumb Company on time and in full. According to the facts found, Environmental Technology Company still has RMB 145,383,568.6 of capital contributions not yet paid to Thumb Company. Environmental Technology Company failed to perform its statutory duty as a shareholder to fully pay its capital contributions, infringing upon the corporate property rights of Thumb Company. Thumb Company has the right to demand that Environmental Technology Company fulfill its capital contribution obligation and make up the shortfall. With respect to the amount of Environmental Technology Company's insufficient capital contribution, Thumb Company in this case only claimed RMB 45 million from Environmental Technology Company. This does not violate the provisions of the law and should be supported.

In summary, in accordance with Article 28, paragraph 1; Article 179, paragraph 1; and Article 218 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 4, paragraph 2 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises; Article 22 of the Implementing Rules for the Law of the People's Republic of China on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises; and Article 13, paragraph 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III), the court rendered the following judgment: Environmental Technology Company shall pay a capital contribution of RMB 45 million to Thumb Company within ten days from the effective date of this judgment. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 266,800 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Environmental Technology Company.

Environmental Technology Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. Bao Guowu is the legally existing current chairman of Thumb Company. The complaint and the power of attorney of Thumb Company were issued by unauthorized persons who misappropriated the company seal. They were not approved by the legal representative and could not represent the true intention of Thumb Company; thus, the lawsuit is invalid. The withdrawal application signed by Bao Guowu represents the true intention of Thumb Company and should be granted. 2. The handling of this case needs to be based on the outcomes of other cases and the result of the capital reduction application; therefore, this case should be stayed and the trial resumed after the relevant facts are ascertained. 3. Thumb Company's renewed request for Environmental Technology Company to fulfill its capital contribution obligation constitutes a repeated lawsuit, violating the principle of "no second action on the same matter," and its complaint should be dismissed. 4. Due to malicious obstruction by the actual controllers of Thumb Company, such as Sun Jiangrong, the capital reduction application was not approved. However, the capital reduction was the true intention of Environmental Technology Company. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of Environmental Technology Company, Thumb Company should comply with the parent company's capital reduction resolution. Its obstructive behavior infringed upon the rights granted to shareholders under the Chinese Company Law. Therefore, Environmental Technology Company requested the revocation of the original judgment, dismissal of Thumb Company's complaint, or permission for Bao Guowu to withdraw the complaint on behalf of Thumb Company. If the foregoing requests could not be supported, it requested a stay of the proceedings in this case or the dismissal of all of Thumb Company's claims.

Thumb Company argued in its defense: 1. Hong Zhen, the legal representative of Thumb Company as recorded in the industrial and commercial registration, has the right to file this lawsuit on behalf of Thumb Company. According to the current laws and regulations of China, the newly appointed legal representative of Thumb Company must be legally registered before exercising the powers of a legal representative. The so-called legal representative Bao Guowu appointed by the judicial manager of Environmental Technology Company has not undergone change registration in accordance with the law, and therefore cannot exercise the powers of a legal representative nor has the authority to apply for withdrawal of the lawsuit. 2. After Environmental Technology Company's previous capital contribution, Thumb Company's request for Environmental Technology Company to fulfill its capital contribution obligation again, based on operational needs and the company's articles of association, does not violate the provisions of the law. Therefore, this lawsuit does not violate the principle of "no second action on the same matter." 3. The reasons for staying the proceedings put forward by Environmental Technology Company are untenable. This case should not be stayed; rather, it should be heard promptly to protect the lawful property rights of Thumb Company. 4. The capital reduction application of Environmental Technology Company must go through the corresponding approval procedures. Before obtaining approval, Environmental Technology Company remains obligated to fulfill its statutory capital contribution obligation. Therefore, it requested the dismissal of the appeal and the affirmation of the original judgment.

During the second-instance trial, both parties to this case explicitly stated that they had no objections to the facts found in the original trial, which this Court hereby confirms.

This Court further finds: On January 20, 2011, the judicial manager of Environmental Technology Company passed a written resolution changing the legal representative of Thumb Company from Tian Yuan to Ho Yuk Kwan, and changing the directors from Tian Yuan, Pan Chengtu, and Chen Bin to Seshadri Rajagopalan, Yu Mingyuan, and Ho Yuk Kwan. On March 30, 2012, the judicial manager of Environmental Technology Company again passed a written resolution and issued an appointment and removal letter, removing Ho Yuk Kwan from the positions of chairman and legal representative of Thumb Company, appointing Bao Guowu as the chairman and legal representative of Thumb Company, removing Seshadri Rajagopalan, Yu Mingyuan, and Ho Yuk Kwan from their director positions at Thumb Company, and appointing Bao Guowu, Xu Liwen, and Song Kuan as directors of Thumb Company, each for a term of three years.

On January 11, 2013, the High Court of Singapore issued winding-up order ORC 336/2013, appointing Hamish Alexander Christie and two others as joint and several liquidators of Environmental Technology Company. The winding-up order stipulated that the liquidators are authorized to exercise any of the powers set out in sections 272(1)(a) to 272(1)(e) of the Companies Act of Singapore.

Section 227G(2) of the Companies Act of Singapore provides that during the period a judicial management order is in force, all the powers of the directors and all the duties of the directors conferred by this Act or by the memorandum or articles of association of the company shall be exercisable and performed by the judicial manager and not by the directors, but nothing in this subsection shall require the judicial manager to convene any meeting of the company.

Section 272(2)(a) of the Companies Act of Singapore provides that the liquidator may bring or defend any action or other legal proceeding in the name and on behalf of the company.

The evidence corresponding to the above facts further found by this Court was already examined during the first-instance trial, and the court of first instance confirmed it but did not find it as established facts.

This Court further finds: On July 19, 2012, while serving as the judicial manager of Environmental Technology Company, Hamish Alexander Christie signed a power of attorney authorizing lawyers Dan Pingyuan and Deng Huiqiong to act as the authorized agents of Environmental Technology Company in all proceedings of this case, including first instance, second instance, and enforcement.

During the second-instance trial, Thumb Company raised an objection to the litigation representation right and the qualification of the authorized agents of Environmental Technology Company, arguing that the liquidators' powers were limited to the scope authorized by the court's winding-up order and did not include the powers stipulated in section 272(2)(a) of the Companies Act of Singapore, and therefore the liquidators were not authorized to represent Environmental Technology Company in this lawsuit.

This Court holds that:

This case is a dispute over shareholder capital contribution involving foreign elements. According to Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-related Civil Relations, which provides that "the civil capacity for rights, civil capacity for conduct, organizational structure, and the rights and obligations of shareholders of a legal person and its branches shall be governed by the law of the place of registration," matters concerning the civil capacity for rights and civil capacity for conduct of the judicial manager and liquidators of Environmental Technology Company shall be governed by the law of the place of registration of Environmental Technology Company, i.e., Singapore law. Matters concerning whether the intention of Thumb Company to file this lawsuit is genuine and the shareholders' obligation to contribute capital shall be governed by Chinese law.

Based on the appeal and defense opinions of both parties and confirmed by both parties, the issues to be adjudicated in this second instance are: 1. whether the litigation representation rights of both parties and the agency qualifications of their agents are valid; 2. whether this case should be stayed; 3. whether the intention of Thumb Company to file this lawsuit is genuine, i.e., whether the legal representative registered with the industrial and commercial administration or the legal representative appointed by the shareholder can represent the will of Thumb Company; 4. whether this case violates the principle of "no second action on the same matter"; 5. whether Environmental Technology Company should fulfill its capital contribution obligation.

I. The issue of whether the litigation representation rights of both parties and the agency qualifications of their agents are valid

Article 48, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that "a legal person shall be represented in litigation by its legal representative." Environmental Technology Company is a Singapore legal person. It has entered into judicial management and winding-up proceedings in accordance with Singapore law. Whether the judicial manager and liquidators of Environmental Technology Company have the authority to represent the company in this lawsuit shall be determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of Singapore law. According to sections 227G(2) and 272(2)(a) of the Companies Act of Singapore, both the judicial manager and the liquidators of Environmental Technology Company have the authority to represent the company in relevant litigation and also have the authority to appoint agents to participate in litigation. Therefore, the objection raised by Thumb Company regarding the litigation representation right of Environmental Technology Company and the qualifications of its agents is untenable.

Thumb Company is a Chinese legal person. It has provided the identification documents of its legal representative as registered with the Chinese administrative authority for industry and commerce and has provided a power of attorney affixed with the company seal of Thumb Company, which complies with the relevant provisions of the Chinese Civil Procedure Law. Therefore, the agents of Thumb Company are entitled to participate in this lawsuit. The objection raised by Environmental Technology Company regarding the qualifications of Thumb Company's agents is also untenable.

II. The issue of whether this case should be stayed

Environmental Technology Company filed several related lawsuits after the acceptance of this case. Although some of those cases involve the issue of whether the legal representative of Thumb Company is qualified, one of the focal points of dispute in this case is whether the legal representative registered with the industrial and commercial administration or the legal representative appointed by the shareholder can represent the will of Thumb Company. Given that Environmental Technology Company has already raised substantive defenses on this issue in this case, the scope of adjudication in this case naturally includes the issue of whether the legal representative of Thumb Company is qualified. This case should make a determination on this issue, and there is no need to rely on the outcomes of other cases. Therefore, there are no circumstances in this case that warrant a stay of proceedings as provided for in the Chinese Civil Procedure Law. Environmental Technology Company's ground of appeal that this case should be stayed is untenable, and its claim in this regard is not supported.

III. The issue of whether the intention of Thumb Company to file this lawsuit is genuine

Thumb Company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established by Environmental Technology Company within the territory of China. According to the relevant provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2005) and the Law of the People's Republic of China on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises and its Implementing Rules, Thumb Company is a one-person company. The right to appoint and remove its internal organizational organs, including directors and the legal representative, is vested in its sole shareholder, Environmental Technology Company.

After Environmental Technology Company entered into judicial management proceedings, the judicial manager passed resolutions to change the directors and legal representative of Thumb Company. According to the relevant provisions of section 227G of the Companies Act of Singapore, during the period of judicial management, the powers and duties of the directors of the company under the Companies Act and the company's articles of association are exercised and performed by the judicial manager. Therefore, the resolutions passed by the judicial manager of Environmental Technology Company should be recognized in this case.

Pursuant to Article 47, item 2 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the board of directors, as the executive organ of the shareholders' meeting, has the obligation to execute the resolutions of the shareholders' meeting or the sole shareholder of the company. The board of directors of Thumb Company should, in accordance with the resolution of its sole shareholder Environmental Technology Company, handle the change of registration of the directors and the legal representative. Because the board of directors of Thumb Company failed to execute the shareholder's resolution, a situation arose where the legal representative registered with the industrial and commercial administration was inconsistent with the legal representative appointed by the shareholder, leading to a dispute. Article 13 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a change of the legal representative of a company shall be registered. This Court holds that the purpose of requiring registration for a change of legal representative under the law is to disclose to the public the basic state of the company's representation of will. The legal representative registered with the industrial and commercial administration has an external effect of public notice. If an external dispute arises concerning the company's representation right involving a third party outside the company, the industrial and commercial registration shall prevail. However, for internal disputes between the company and its shareholders arising from the appointment or removal of the legal representative, the effective resolution of the shareholders' meeting shall prevail, and the legal effect of the change of legal representative shall arise within the company. Therefore, the resolution of Environmental Technology Company, as the sole shareholder of Thumb Company, appointing the legal representative of Thumb Company is binding on Thumb Company.

At the time of the filing of this lawsuit, Environmental Technology Company had already replaced the legal representative of Thumb Company. The newly appointed legal representative of Thumb Company explicitly expressed opposition to Thumb Company filing this lawsuit. Therefore, the filing of this lawsuit does not represent the true intention of Thumb Company and should be dismissed. Environmental Technology Company's ground of appeal that the filing of this lawsuit was not the true intention of Thumb Company is well-founded.

Given that Thumb Company's complaint should be dismissed, there is no need to further adjudicate on issues such as whether Bao Guowu's application to withdraw the lawsuit on behalf of Thumb Company should be granted, whether this case violates the principle of "no second action on the same matter," and whether Environmental Technology Company should fulfill its capital contribution obligation.

In summary, Environmental Technology Company's grounds of appeal are well-founded, and its appeal requests are supported by this Court. The original judgment applied the law incorrectly and should be revoked. In accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 186 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

1. The civil judgment of the Fujian High People's Court (2013) Min Min Chu Zi No. 43 is hereby revoked;

2. The complaint of Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd. is hereby dismissed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 266,800 is to be refunded to Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd. The property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 is to be borne by Thumb Environmental Technology Group (Fujian) Co., Ltd. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 266,800 is to be refunded to Sino-Environmental Technology Group Co., Ltd.

This ruling is final.
